recipes.name: Easy Apple Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.1 ounce) package pastry for a 9-inch double-crust pie
0.75 cup white sugar, or more to taste

steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).
Line a 9-inch pie dish with one pastry crust; set second one aside.
Combine 3/4 cup sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl. Add more sugar if your apples are tart.
Layer apple slices in the prepared pie dish, sprinkling each layer with cinnamon-sugar mixture.
Dot top layer with small pieces of butter. Cover with top crust and flute the edges to seal.
Beat egg with 1 tablespoon water to make an egg wash; brush the top crust with egg wash. Cut several slits in the top crust to allow steam to escape.

Bake pie on the lowest rack of the preheated oven for 10 minutes. Reduce oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and continue baking until golden brown and filling bubbles, 30 to 35 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Apple Pie
raw_recipe.description: This super easy apple pie recipe simply fills a double-crust pie with layers of apples and cinnamon sugar for a warm and irresistible fall dessert.

video.description: Nothing says fall has arrived quite like a freshly baked apple pie. In this video, Nicole shows you how to make three decadent apple pie recipes; a classic apple pie, the easiest apple pie, and a caramel apple crisp pie!
video.name: How to Make Apple Pie, 3 Ways

review.reviewBody: This is a wonderful recipe. I added 1-2 TBLS lemon jiuce, 2 TBLS flour, 1/2 teas vanilla 1/4 teas nutmeg and used brown sugar instead of white. Then mixed the seasonings with the apples before putting it in the crust. I won first prize at a local Farmer's Market apple pie contest so thanks! I cooked it longer- more like 55 minutes so next time will do the 10 minutes at 450, then 40 minutes at 375 I think will work great. It might be my stove so just wait until it is bubbling.

I have made this pie several times to the point of not needing the recipe anymore. Even though it's simple, people rave over it! 

I recently began to add 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract, and it gives a wonderful flavor. Also, I spray my pie pan with Butter flavored nonstick spray, so it's easy to serve (I do cheat and use the refrigerated crusts).

I like to dash the crust with a little butter, sugar, and cinnamon.

Made own butter, flaky crust & one step that MUST be used to prevent a watery, soggy bottom crust—butter the bottom pie pan BEFORE adding your crust to the pan. This simple step will prevent soggy crust from pie liquids. Thanks for the recipe.

I made this recipe for Christmas Eve with a pre-teen in the family. It was easy for her to follow with made the process enjoyable. I didn't need as many apple as I didn't want to create a mountain of apples at the center. I used 4 large organic Granny Smith apples. I reviewed the comments below and made a few adjustments: 1) brushed the rim of the bottom crust with egg, 2) create vents (or holes for ventilation), 3) brushed the top crust with a bit of egg and (almond) milk. Everyone loved it! Even one of the kids said it's better (in taste and smell) than store bought.

Came out delicious!!! I changed the recipe a little bit. I put a whole stick of butter with sunflower oil in a pan on very low heat, with cinnamon, nutmeg and allspice, and a small amount of granulated sugar. I whisked it to a perfect spice sauce, poured the thinly sliced apples in and tossed them in the butter sauce. Then I let the mixture cool for a few minutes while I prepared the premade dough into the pie dish. I also sprinkled a little more cinnamon on to the unbaked dough, placed apples on top, with small amounts of butter on top of apples, placed top crust, melted butter and sprinkled granulated sugar on top. Baked according to directions.

I love this recipe. I did modify it slightly. I added a mounded tablespoon of flour and then cinnamon and a little nutmeg. I mixed everything thing in a bowl and then tossed with the apples to get them evenly coated. I use half Granny Smith and half Johnathon apples. It makes a great flavor. I would also cover your crust with a pie crust shield and remove it the last 15-20 minutes.

I was skeptical about trying this recipe at first, but I needed a quick dessert for the Fourth of July and I had a plethora of Granny Smith apples left. The recipe is a simple one, but I tweaked it a little bit. I added a couple of dashes of nutmeg, used 1/4 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup white sugar. I also added two teaspoons of cornstarch to help thicken the juices a bit. I made the "Butter Flaky Crust" the day before. As for baking, I started it off at 450 degrees for ten minutes then reduced the temp to 350 and let it bake for about thirty-five minutes. It's important to make sure the juices are bubbly before removing from the oven.

PS-Brush the crust with one egg mixed with a tablespoon of water to make it nice and brown. (Makes for great presentation)

Great recipe especially for my first time making Apple pie. I read extensively through the reviews: I added 1/2 cup brown sugar, 2 TBL flour, 3/4 teaspoon ground cloves to mixture. I mixed it all in a gallon ziploc and tosses until evenly coated. I layered the mixture with several tablespoons of unsalted butter. I chose Braeburn apples, 6 did the trick and they were perfect (a bit tart but plenty sweet, perfectly balanced.) I also did a 1 egg white and 2 tablespoons milk mix to brush on top of final pie crust, sprinkled white sugar on top. I covered the edge of pie with foil for 40 minutes of bake time, and added turned the heat up to 375 for 20 more minutes at the end of bake time. Also let it sit for 10 additional minutes with the oven off. Lots of modifications but you guys it was DELICIOUS!!!!

This was my first experience making apple pie and I loved that this recipe was so simple. Following the advice of other members I added 3TBSP white flour and nutmeg to the sugar and cinnamon mixture (I also used brown sugar instead of white since that's what we use at home). Once that was done I tossed the apple with the mixture (also suggested) and brushed the top with an egg wash made with an egg and some milk. I finished by sprinkling the top with some sugar. The pie was gorgeous!!!! This is definitely my new favorite dessert to make because of how beautiful it looks and smells :-)

This was a nice apple pie recipe. I made it my own with a few change: I added 1 teaspoon nutmeg (I like nutmeg) and reduced the cinnamon you 1/2 teaspoon, cut my apples into chunks instead of slices, and took out 2 tablespoons sugar and replaced with 2-3 tablespoons of flour. 

My instructional changes were: In a large bowl I combined sugar, flour, nutmeg, and cinnamon and mixed well. I stirred @ 1/3 of the apples in the mixture and coated well and placed in the pie shell and repeated with the remaining 2/3 of the apples. 

With just a few ingredients, this was a quick and easy pie that was very tasty.
It's a good recipe just a little runny so I put 2 tablespoons of cornstarch and thickened it up was great

So easy to make. I love the simple apples and cinnamon sugar layers with butter on top. I used king Arthur pie crust mix which made it much easier and fast. Peeling and slicing was the longest time but my husband helped and my puppy ate some apple peelings.
Easy. Thanks
Flour or something to thicken any liquid. I'm so glad that I read the comments and it was mentioned. So I put in 3 tbsp flour.
It turned out to be a wateree mess been so long since I been able to bake I didn't notice it didn't have a thinking in it fantastic taste just needed tweaking
smelled great but very runny
I love making homemade apple pie now love your recipes
Really easy. Good way to use up apples!
Flour is not mentioned. The pie is like a soup. Awful

Made it almost exactly as written. Used all brown sugar instead of white. Baked longer than was written. Needed about 10 more minutes. Left the skin on the apples. Delicious. I plan on using this recipe for Thanksgiving
